notes: Schematic WGS84 extents for Europa Strata time-slider overlays — NOT modern state borders. Polygons are research-informed approximations of high-medieval polities (kingdoms, major duchies, leagues, tribal confederations). Feudal mosaics (France, HRE, Italy) are simplified to dominant or collective extents; overseas colonies are often omitted or noted. Sources: Euratlas century maps, Shepherd/standard atlas tradition, and secondary syntheses of Capetian, Hohenstaufen, Reconquista, Crusade, Mongol, and Baltic crusade geopolitics.

polities.name: Kingdom of England

1000.notes: Æthelred’s England; Danelaw imprint; excludes Scotland/Wales cores.

1100.notes: Norman kingdom; Marcher pressure on Wales; Scotland separate.

1200.notes: Plantagenet England island core; Angevin continental lands mapped separately.

1300.notes: Edwardian England including conquered Wales; Scotland contested.

1400.notes: Lancastrian England; Wales incorporated; HYW continental claims fluid.

polities.description: Late Anglo-Saxon kingdom under Æthelred II faces renewed Danish pressure, then Cnut’s North Sea empire (1016–35). Norman Conquest (1066) remakes the elite: Domesday Book, castles, feudal tenures. Angevin kings (Henry II) build a cross-Channel realm; John’s loss of Normandy (1204) and Magna Carta (1215) redefine kingship. Edward I conquers Wales; Scotland wars follow. Hundred Years’ War (from 1337) projects English power into France under Edward III and Henry V, then Lancastrian crisis after 1399.
polities.conflicts: Vikings/Danes; Scotland; Wales; France (HYW); Ireland lordship wars.
polities.leaders: Æthelred II; Cnut; William I; Henry II; John; Edward I; Edward III; Henry V; Richard II
polities.religion: Latin Christianity (Roman rite); monastic reform; later mendicant orders.
polities.culture: Old English → Middle English; Norman French elite; common law; shire administration.

polities.description: Alba consolidates Gaelic and Pictish inheritances; Canmore dynasty anglicizes court and burghs while Norse power lingers in the Isles. Wars of Independence (Wallace, Bruce) after 1296 assert sovereignty vs Edwardian England; Declaration of Arbroath (1320). Later Stewart kings balance Highland clans, Lowland burghs, and English diplomacy.

polities.leaders: Malcolm II; Macbeth; Malcolm III; William the Lion; Robert I Bruce; David II; Robert II
polities.religion: Latin Christianity; Culdee memory giving way to diocesan church.
polities.culture: Gaelic Highlands; Scots/English Lowlands; Norse Atlantic fringe.

polities.description: Fragmented Welsh kingdoms (Gwynedd, Powys, Deheubarth) under princes negotiating with Norman Marcher lords. Llywelyn the Great and Llywelyn ap Gruffudd briefly unify much of Wales before Edward I’s conquest (1277–83) and Statute of Rhuddlan.

polities.leaders: Gruffudd ap Llywelyn; Owain Gwynedd; Llywelyn the Great; Llywelyn ap Gruffudd

polities.description: Gaelic túatha and provincial kings (Uí Néill, Munster, Connacht, Leinster) share the island with Norse-Gaelic towns. Brian Boru’s Clontarf (1014) is a hinge. Anglo-Norman invasion (1169–71) creates the Lordship of Ireland under the English crown, never fully subduing the Gaelic west and north; by 1400 a hybrid Pale / Gaelic Ireland pattern dominates.
polities.conflicts: Norse towns; Anglo-Norman barons; English crown.
polities.leaders: Brian Boru; Ruaidrí Ua Conchobair; Strongbow; later Gaelic and Anglo-Irish lords
polities.religion: Latin Christianity (synods reforming older Irish church); saints’ cults.

polities.name: Capetian / Valois France

1000.notes: Capetian royal orbit around Île-de-France; great fiefs dwarf demesne.

1100.notes: Still feudal mosaic; Capetians expanding influence vs Normandy/Anjou.

1200.notes: Philip II era: royal power rising; Occitan south still contested.

1300.notes: Post-Albigensian & Capetian consolidation; Languedoc absorbed.

1400.notes: Valois France in HYW; Burgundy & English footholds carve the west/north.

polities.description: Hugh Capet’s line begins with a small demesne around Paris amid mighty princes (Normandy, Flanders, Aquitaine, Toulouse). Twelfth–thirteenth centuries: Philip II Augustus breaks Angevin power, Louis IX sacralizes Capetian justice, Philip IV confronts the papacy. Albigensian Crusade integrates the Occitan south. Valois branch fights the Hundred Years’ War; by 1400 Burgundy is a dangerous appanage rival while English hold Normandy/Gascony intermittently.
polities.conflicts: England/Angevins; Flanders; Empire; Occitan lords; later Burgundy & England in HYW.
polities.leaders: Hugh Capet; Philip I; Louis VI; Philip II; Louis IX; Philip IV; Charles V; Charles VI
polities.religion: Latin Christianity; Cluny/Cistercians; universities (Paris); Avignon papacy era overlap.
polities.culture: Old French; feudal hierarchy → royal officers (baillis); Gothic architecture.

polities.name: Duchy of Normandy

1000.notes: Duchy of Normandy; launching pad for 1066.

1100.notes: Duchy of Normandy; launching pad for 1066.

polities.description: Scandinavian-settled duchy under Rollo’s heirs becomes a Latin-Christian powerhouse. William conquers England (1066); thereafter Normandy is usually held with the English crown until Philip II confiscates it from John (1204). Ducal administration, cavalry, and monastic patronage set models for Anglo-Norman rule.
polities.conflicts: Capetian kings; Anjou; Brittany; England after 1066 as dual realm.
polities.leaders: Richard I of Normandy; Robert the Magnificent; William the Conqueror; Henry I; later Angevin dukes
polities.culture: Norman French; castles; feudal knight service.

polities.name: Angevin / Plantagenet continental lands

1200.notes: Henry II / Richard / John continental Angevin bloc before 1204 collapse.

polities.description: Henry II’s inheritance and marriage to Eleanor of Aquitaine create a cross-Channel assemblage: England, Normandy, Anjou, Maine, Touraine, Aquitaine—often called the Angevin Empire though not a centralized state. Richard I’s absence and John’s failures let Philip II dismantle the northern continental bloc after 1202–04; Gascony lingers as a HYW flashpoint.
polities.conflicts: Capetian France; Brittany; Toulouse; Welsh/Scottish fronts via England.
polities.leaders: Henry II; Richard I Lionheart; John
polities.religion: Latin Christianity; Plantagenet sacral kingship claims.
polities.culture: Anglo-Norman French elites; diverse customary laws per province.

polities.name: Valois Burgundy

1400.notes: Valois Burgundy: Flanders–Brabant + duchy; HYW third force.

polities.description: Philip the Bold’s appanage grows into a composite Low Countries–Burgundy state under Philip the Bold and John the Fearless. At 1400 it is the third force of the Hundred Years’ War, balancing between England and Valois France, with rich Flemish cities and a glittering court culture.
polities.conflicts: Valois France; England; Liège; Swiss later.
polities.leaders: Philip the Bold; John the Fearless
polities.religion: Latin Christianity; court chapels; urban confraternities.
polities.culture: French/Flemish bilingual courts; luxury cloth cities; chivalric orders.

polities.name: Holy Roman Empire

1000.notes: Ottonian Reich: German stem duchies + Kingdom of Italy claim; Bohemia tributary.

1100.notes: Salian HRE; Investiture Contest; Arelat/Burgundy orbit.

1200.notes: Hohenstaufen high point under Frederick I/II claims; communal Italy restless.

1300.notes: Post-Interregnum; electors; weaker Italian grip.

1400.notes: Luxemburg/Habsburg era; Swiss cantons peeling west edge.

polities.description: Ottonian and Salian emperors claim Rome and the German stem duchies plus the Kingdom of Italy; Bohemia is a privileged realm inside the orbit. Investiture Contest (Canossa 1077) reshapes papacy–empire relations. Hohenstaufen (Frederick I Barbarossa, Frederick II) fight Lombard communes and popes. Great Interregnum (1250–73) weakens central power; Golden Bull (1356) fixes electors. By 1400 the Reich is a legal umbrella over princes, free cities, and Habsburg/Luxemburg dynasts—not a unitary state.
polities.conflicts: Papacy; Lombard League; France; Magyars early; Italy communes; Swiss.
polities.leaders: Otto III; Henry II; Henry IV; Frederick I; Frederick II; Rudolf of Habsburg; Charles IV
polities.religion: Latin Christianity; imperial church (Reichskirche); later conciliarism.
polities.culture: German vernaculars + Latin chancery; feudal princes; free imperial cities.

polities.name: Duchy / Kingdom of Bohemia

1000.notes: Přemyslid Bohemia within/alongside the Reich.

1100.notes: Přemyslid Bohemia within/alongside the Reich.

1200.notes: Přemyslid Bohemia within/alongside the Reich.

1300.notes: Přemyslid Bohemia within/alongside the Reich.

1400.notes: Přemyslid Bohemia within/alongside the Reich.

polities.description: Přemyslid Bohemia is baptized and tied to the Reich yet retains strong dukes/kings. Ottokar II expands aggressively in the 13th century; Luxemburg dynasty (Charles IV) makes Prague an imperial capital. Hussite storm follows after 1400.
polities.conflicts: Empire; Hungary; Poland; Austria (Ottokar vs Rudolf).
polities.leaders: Boleslaus I; Vratislaus II; Ottokar II; Wenceslaus II; Charles IV
polities.culture: Czech language elite; German settlers in towns/mines; silver of Kutná Hora.

polities.name: Piast / reunited Poland

1000.notes: Piast realm under Bolesław Chrobry — peak early expansion.

1100.notes: Piast kingdom after Bolesław III; later fragmentation brewing.

1200.notes: Fragmented duchies (Seniorate principle); map shows Polish lands collectively.

1300.notes: Władysław Łokietek reunification underway; Casimir III expansion soon.

1400.notes: Kingdom of Poland in personal union with Lithuania (Krewo 1385).

polities.description: Mieszko I’s baptism (966) and Bolesław Chrobry’s coronation ambitions define early Piast power. Twelfth-century fragmentation into duchies weakens the kingdom versus Brandenburg and the Teutonic Order. Władysław Łokietek reunites a core; Casimir III expands and codifies. Krewo (1385) and Jadwiga–Jogaila create the Poland–Lithuania personal union fighting the Order (Grunwald 1410 soon after 1400).
polities.conflicts: Empire; Bohemia; Teutonic Order; Lithuania (then union); Mongols 1241.
polities.leaders: Mieszko I; Bolesław I; Bolesław III; Władysław Łokietek; Casimir III; Jadwiga; Władysław II Jagiełło
polities.religion: Latin Christianity; dioceses of Gniezno orbit.
polities.culture: Polish Piast elite; German town law (Magdeburg); rural colonization.

polities.name: Kingdom of Hungary

1000.notes: Stephen I’s Christian kingdom in the Carpathian Basin.

1100.notes: Árpád Hungary; Croatia union from 1102 expands Adriatic claim.

1200.notes: Árpád high medieval kingdom incl. Croatia–Dalmatia claims.

1300.notes: Anjou Hungary rising after Árpád extinction (1301).

1400.notes: Sigismund-era Hungary; Balkan buffer vs Ottomans.

polities.description: Stephen I crowns a Christian Árpád kingdom in the Carpathian Basin. Croatia enters personal union (1102). Mongol invasion (1241–42) devastates the plain; Béla IV rebuilds with stone castles and settlers. Árpád line ends 1301; Angevins (Charles Robert, Louis the Great) restore strength. Sigismund faces Ottoman advance after Kosovo (1389) and Nicopolis (1396).
polities.conflicts: Byzantium; Holy Roman Empire; Bohemia; Mongols; Ottomans; Venice (Dalmatia).
polities.leaders: Stephen I; Ladislaus I; Béla III; Béla IV; Charles Robert; Louis I; Sigismund
polities.religion: Latin Christianity; Greek rite minorities; later dual pressures.
polities.culture: Magyar nobility; Latin chancery; multiethnic kingdom (Slavs, Germans, Vlachs).

polities.name: Kingdom of Croatia

1000.notes: Kingdom of Croatia before 1102 union with Hungary.

polities.description: Trpimirović Croatia straddles Adriatic and inland zones, balancing Byzantium, Venice, and Hungary. After dynastic crisis, the 1102 pact (pacta conventa tradition) joins Croatia to the Hungarian crown while retaining separate institutions.
polities.conflicts: Venice; Byzantium; Hungary; Bulgaria.
polities.leaders: Tomislav; Krešimir IV; Zvonimir; later bans under Hungary
polities.culture: Croatian Slavic elite; Dalmatian coastal towns.

polities.name: Kingdom of Denmark

1000.notes: Jutland + Danish isles; Skåne/Halland/Blekinge often Danish.

1100.notes: Denmark with Scanian provinces.

1200.notes: Denmark with Scanian provinces.

1300.notes: Denmark with Scanian provinces.

1400.notes: Denmark with Scanian provinces.

polities.description: Bluetooth’s conversion claim and Cnut’s empire make Denmark a North Sea power. Later Valdemars expand into the southern Baltic and Estonia; 13th–14th c. crises precede Margaret I’s Kalmar Union (1397) uniting Scandinavia under a Danish-led crown.
polities.conflicts: Empire/Saxony; Norway; Sweden; Wendish coasts; later Holstein.
polities.leaders: Harold Bluetooth; Swein Forkbeard; Cnut; Valdemar I; Valdemar II; Margaret I
polities.culture: Danish vernacular; North Sea trade; Scanian markets.

polities.name: Kingdom of Norway

1000.notes: Coastal kingdom; Norse Atlantic (Orkney/Hebrides) influence early.

1300.notes: Coastal kingdom; Norse Atlantic (Orkney/Hebrides) influence early.

1400.notes: Coastal kingdom; Norse Atlantic (Orkney/Hebrides) influence early.

polities.description: Unification under fairhair traditions and missionary kings (Olaf Tryggvason, St Olaf) Christianizes the realm. Civil wars give way to Sverre and Håkon IV’s high medieval kingdom with Atlantic possessions (Iceland submission 1262–64, Greenland, Isles earlier). Black Death and unions pull Norway toward Denmark by 1400.
polities.conflicts: Denmark; Scotland (Hebrides); internal claimants; later Kalmar politics.
polities.leaders: Olaf Tryggvason; Olaf Haraldsson; Harald Hardrada; Sverre; Håkon IV; Magnus VI
polities.religion: Latin Christianity; saint-king cult of Olaf.
polities.culture: Old Norse; coastal lagting; Atlantic diaspora.

polities.name: Kingdom of Sweden

1000.notes: Svealand–Götaland consolidation; Finland not yet held.

1100.notes: Svealand–Götaland consolidation; Finland not yet held.

1200.notes: Sweden expanding into Finland; Birger Jarl era framing.

1300.notes: Sweden expanding into Finland; Birger Jarl era framing.

1400.notes: Swedish realm in/against Kalmar Union.

polities.description: Svear and Götar polities Christianize unevenly; Eric Saints and Birger Jarl frame a kingdom that crusades into Finland. Folkung dynasty, then unions and revolts against Danish-led Kalmar after 1397. Stockholm and mining districts rise in the later Middle Ages.
polities.conflicts: Denmark; Novgorod (Karelian frontier); Norway; pagan Baltic holdouts early.
polities.leaders: Olof Skötkonung; Eric IX; Birger Jarl; Magnus Ladulås; Margaret I (union); Engelbrekt later
polities.religion: Latin Christianity spreading from the southwest.
polities.culture: Old Swedish; ting assemblies; Finnish marches.

polities.name: Kalmar Union

1400.notes: Kalmar Union (1397): Denmark–Norway–Sweden under one crown (contested).

polities.description: Margaret I unites Denmark, Norway, and Sweden at Kalmar (1397) under one monarch to counter German Hansa and aristocratic fragmentation. Swedish resistance repeatedly strains the union; at 1400 the structure still holds under Eric of Pomerania.
polities.conflicts: Hansa; Holstein; Swedish nobles; Teutonic Baltic politics.
polities.leaders: Margaret I; Eric of Pomerania
polities.culture: Scandinavian vernaculars; shared dynastic court vs local councils.

polities.name: León–Castile / Crown of Castile

1000.notes: León–Castile Christian north; frontier south of Duero shifting.

1100.notes: Castile–León after Toledo (1085); Almoravid counter-pressure.

1200.notes: Castile after Las Navas (1212) push; Almohad south shrinking.

1300.notes: Crown of Castile dominant Meseta; Granada remains Muslim south.

1400.notes: Crown of Castile dominant Meseta; Granada remains Muslim south.

polities.description: Astur-Leonese inheritance becomes Castile–León, spearhead of the northern Reconquista. Toledo falls 1085; Almoravid and Almohad reactions reverse gains until Las Navas de Tolosa (1212). Fernando III and Alfonso X consolidate a Castilian Meseta crown; Granada remains the last Andalusi emirate. Dynastic crises (Trastámara) mark the 14th century.
polities.conflicts: Andalusi states; Navarre; Aragon; Portugal; internal magnates.
polities.leaders: Sancho III orbit; Alfonso VI; Alfonso VII; Fernando III; Alfonso X; Alfonso XI
polities.religion: Latin Christianity; Mozarabic communities; military orders (Santiago, Calatrava).
polities.culture: Castilian Romance; frontier society (presura); convivencia pressures.

polities.name: Crown of Aragon

1100.notes: Aragon + Catalonia emerging Mediterranean crown.

1200.notes: Crown of Aragon; Balearics soon (1229+).

1300.notes: Aragon: mainland + Balearics + Sicily after Sicilian Vespers.

1400.notes: Aragon Mediterranean composite: Catalonia–Aragon–Valencia–Balearics–Sardinia–Sicily.

polities.description: Aragon and Catalonia unite under Ramon Berenguer IV / Petronilla line, then conquer Valencia and the Balearics. Mediterranean expansion (Sicily after 1282 Vespers, Sardinia) makes a composite thalassocratic crown balancing Cortes and urban commerce (Barcelona).
polities.conflicts: Castile; France (Occitan); Angevin Naples/Sicily; Genoa; Muslim Valencia/Balearics.
polities.leaders: Ramiro I; Alfonso I the Battler; James I; Peter III; Alfonso V later
polities.culture: Catalan–Aragonese languages; consulates of the sea; Mediterranean trade.

polities.name: Kingdom of Navarre

1000.notes: Kingdom of Navarre / Pamplona.

1100.notes: Kingdom of Navarre / Pamplona.

1200.notes: Kingdom of Navarre / Pamplona.

1300.notes: Kingdom of Navarre / Pamplona.

1400.notes: Kingdom of Navarre / Pamplona.

polities.description: Pyrenean Basque-rooted kingdom of Pamplona/Navarre punches above its size under Sancho III, then is squeezed between Castile, Aragon, and France. Capetian and later French dynastic ties pull it northward while retaining distinct fueros.
polities.conflicts: Castile; Aragon; France; Andalusi neighbors early.
polities.leaders: Sancho III the Great; García Ramírez; Sancho VI; later Champenois/Capetian dynasts
polities.culture: Basque and Romance; customary fueros.

polities.name: Kingdom of Portugal

1100.notes: County → kingdom under Afonso Henriques (recognized 1143/1179).

1200.notes: Portugal to the Algarve frontier after Reconquista push.

1300.notes: Stabilized Portuguese Atlantic kingdom.

1400.notes: Stabilized Portuguese Atlantic kingdom.

polities.description: County of Portugal under Henry of Burgundy’s line becomes a kingdom under Afonso Henriques, recognized by León and the papacy. Southward conquest reaches the Algarve in the 13th century. Aviz dynasty (from 1385, Aljubarrota) secures independence from Castile; Atlantic orientation intensifies after 1400.
polities.conflicts: Castile–León; Almohads; later Castile (1383–85 crisis).
polities.leaders: Afonso Henriques; Sancho I; Afonso III; Dinis; João I
polities.culture: Portuguese Romance; Atlantic ports; Reconquista frontier.

polities.name: Andalusi Córdoba / taifas

1000.notes: Late Córdoba / early taifa patchwork — mapped as Andalusi south.

polities.description: Umayyad Córdoba’s fitna after 1009 fragments the caliphate into taifa kingdoms (Seville, Toledo, Zaragoza, Granada, etc.) by 1031—rich but militarily weak vs Christian north, inviting Maghrebi interventions.
polities.conflicts: León–Castile; Navarre; Catalonia; Berber factions.
polities.leaders: Hisham II; Almanzor (hajib power); taifa kings (Abbadids, etc.)
polities.religion: Sunni Islam; Jewish and Christian dhimmi communities; Arabic high culture.
polities.culture: Arabic; Mozarabic Romance; Hebrew poetry; courtly learning.

polities.name: Almoravid Empire (Iberian edge)

1100.notes: Almoravid Maghreb–Andalus empire edge in Iberia c. 1100.

polities.description: Sanhaja Berber reform empire from the Maghreb answers Andalusi pleas after Toledo’s fall, winning Sagrajas (1086) and reuniting much of Muslim Iberia under austere Maliki rule before Almohad overthrow.
polities.conflicts: Castile; Aragon; taifa remnants; rising Almohads.
polities.leaders: Yusuf ibn Tashfin; Ali ibn Yusuf
polities.culture: Berber–Andalusi Arabic administration; Maghrebi military.

polities.name: Almohad Caliphate (Iberian edge)

1200.notes: Almohad south after mid-12th c.; collapsing after 1212.

polities.description: Masmuda Almohads replace Almoravids, briefly dominating al-Andalus and the Maghreb. Las Navas de Tolosa (1212) breaks their Iberian spine; successor third taifas and Nasrid Granada follow.
polities.conflicts: Castile; Aragon; Portugal; internal revolts.
polities.leaders: Abd al-Mu'min; Yaqub al-Mansur; Muhammad al-Nasir
polities.religion: Almohad tawhid doctrine → later Maliki normalization.
polities.culture: Maghrebi–Andalusi urban culture; fortified frontiers.

polities.name: Nasrid Granada

1300.notes: Nasrid Emirate of Granada (from 1230s).

1400.notes: Nasrid Emirate of Granada (from 1230s).

polities.description: Last Muslim state in Iberia under the Nasrids, surviving as a tributary/cultural powerhouse (Alhambra) between Castile and the Maghreb until 1492.
polities.conflicts: Castile; Morocco; internal Nasrid factions.
polities.leaders: Muhammad I ibn al-Ahmar; Yusuf I; Muhammad V
polities.culture: Andalusi Arabic; irrigated agriculture; craft luxury.

polities.name: Byzantine Empire

1000.notes: Macedonian Byzantium apex: Balkans + Anatolia core (schematic).

1100.notes: Komnenian recovery after Manzikert losses; Anatolia partly Seljuk.

1200.notes: Post-1204 successor states: Nicaea, Epirus, Trebizond.

1300.notes: Palaiologan restored empire — shrinking vs Turks & Balkans.

1400.notes: Byzantine rump: Constantinople, Morea fragments, a few islands.

polities.description: Macedonian dynasty apex under Basil II conquers Bulgaria (1018). Manzikert (1071) opens Anatolia to Turks; Komnenoi recover partially. Fourth Crusade (1204) shatters the empire into Latin and Greek successor states; Michael VIII restores Constantinople (1261). Palaiologoi preside over a shrinking rump pressed by Serbs, Bulgarians, and Ottomans—by 1400 little more than the capital and fragments.
polities.conflicts: Bulgaria; Normans; Seljuks; Crusaders; Venice; Ottomans; Serbia.
polities.leaders: Basil II; Alexios I; Manuel I; Theodore I Laskaris; Michael VIII; John V; Manuel II
polities.culture: Greek Roman law/culture; thematic → pronoia military society; urban Constantinople.

polities.name: First Bulgarian Empire

1000.notes: First Bulgarian Empire — final phase before Basil II conquest (1018).

polities.description: Samuel’s Bulgaria resists Basil II until total conquest (1018). At 1000 it still controls much of the western Balkans as Byzantium’s great rival.
polities.conflicts: Byzantium; Magyars; Croats; Serbs.
polities.leaders: Samuel of Bulgaria
polities.culture: South Slavic elite; Preslav/Ohrid literary tradition.

polities.name: Second Bulgarian Empire

1200.notes: Second Bulgarian Empire after Asen revolt (1185+).

1300.notes: Second Bulgaria declining vs Serbia & Byzantium.

polities.description: Asen–Peter revolt restores a Bulgarian tsardom centered on Tarnovo. Ivan Asen II’s mid-13th-century peak fades under Mongol pressure, Serbian competition, and Ottoman conquest of the 1390s.
polities.conflicts: Byzantium; Latin Empire; Serbia; Hungary; Mongols; Ottomans.
polities.leaders: Ivan Asen I; Kaloyan; Ivan Asen II; Ivan Alexander
polities.culture: Tarnovo culture; Slavic chancery.

polities.name: Serbian lands / empire

1200.notes: Raška / Nemanjić Serbian lands consolidating.

1300.notes: Serbian kingdom expanding under Milutin; Dušan empire mid-century.

1400.notes: Serbian lands after empire; Ottoman vassalage rising.

polities.description: Stefan Nemanja’s heirs build an Orthodox kingdom; Stefan Dušan’s mid-14th-century empire briefly dominates the central Balkans before fragmentation. After Kosovo (1389) Serbian lords become Ottoman vassals; a despotate persists into the 15th century.
polities.conflicts: Byzantium; Bulgaria; Hungary; Ottomans; Venice (coast).
polities.leaders: Stefan Nemanja; Stefan the First-Crowned; Stefan Dušan; Lazar Hrebeljanović; Stefan Lazarević
polities.culture: Slavic chancery; hill fortresses; mining towns (Novo Brdo).

polities.name: Latin Empire & Frankish Greece

1200.notes: Latin Empire of Constantinople (1204–1261) + Frankish Greece orbit.

polities.description: Fourth Crusade installs a Latin emperor in Constantinople with vassal principalities (Achaea, Athens) and Venetian privileges. Greeks of Nicaea reclaim the city in 1261; Frankish Morea lingers.
polities.conflicts: Nicaea; Bulgaria; Epirus; Venice; Seljuks.
polities.leaders: Baldwin I; Henry of Flanders; later Latin claimants
polities.religion: Latin Catholicism imposed over Orthodox population.
polities.culture: French feudal imports; Venetian trade colonies.

polities.name: Ottoman Sultanate

1300.notes: Early Ottoman beylik in NW Anatolia; Gallipoli 1354 soon.

1400.notes: Ottoman Rumelia: Thrace, Bulgaria, Macedonia; Serbia/Wallachia pressured.

polities.description: Osman’s beylik in Bithynia expands under Orhan and Murad I into Thrace and the Balkans (Adrianople capital). Kosovo (1389) and Nicopolis (1396) mark European crisis; Bayezid I’s rise is checked by Timur at Ankara (1402), temporarily fragmenting the state.
polities.conflicts: Byzantium; Serbia; Bulgaria; Hungary; Timur; Anatolian beyliks.
polities.leaders: Osman I; Orhan; Murad I; Bayezid I
polities.religion: Sunni Islam; dervish frontiers; Christian rayah populations.
polities.culture: Ghazi warrior ethos; early Janissary institutions; multiethnic Rumelia.

polities.name: Sultanate of Rum

1100.notes: Sultanate of Rum in Anatolia after Manzikert settlement.

1200.notes: Sultanate of Rum in Anatolia after Manzikert settlement.

polities.description: Turkish sultanate in Anatolia after Manzikert, capital often Iconium (Konya). Trades and wars with Byzantium and crusaders; Mongol defeat at Köse Dağ (1243) makes it a vassal before beylik fragmentation (including Ottomans).
polities.conflicts: Byzantium; Crusader states; Danishmends; Mongols; Cilician Armenia.
polities.leaders: Suleiman ibn Qutalmish; Kilij Arslan II; Kayqubad I
polities.culture: Turcoman settlement; caravanserais; Anatolian towns.

polities.name: Papal States

1000.notes: Papal States / Patrimonium Petri — Rome to Ravenna corridor schematic.

1100.notes: Papal States / Patrimonium Petri — Rome to Ravenna corridor schematic.

1200.notes: Papal States / Patrimonium Petri — Rome to Ravenna corridor schematic.

1300.notes: Papal States / Patrimonium Petri — Rome to Ravenna corridor schematic.

1400.notes: Papal States / Patrimonium Petri — Rome to Ravenna corridor schematic.

polities.description: Bishop of Rome’s temporal Patrimonium in central Italy, oscillating with imperial protection and communal Rome. Gregorian Reform and Investiture Contest assert papal monarchy; 13th-century peaks under Innocent III. Avignon period (1309–77) relocates the curia to France; Western Schism follows.
polities.conflicts: Holy Roman Emperors; Norman/Sicilian kings; communal Rome; later Avignon politics.
polities.leaders: Sylvester II; Gregory VII; Urban II; Innocent III; Boniface VIII; later Avignon popes
polities.religion: Latin Catholicism; reform papacy; mendicant approval.
polities.culture: Latin curia; pilgrimage economy; patchwork vassals.

polities.name: Islamic Sicily

1000.notes: Kalbid / late Islamic Sicily c. 1000.

polities.description: Kalbid and later fractured Muslim Sicily remains a rich Mediterranean granary and cultural crossroads until Norman conquest (1061–91) under the Hautevilles.
polities.conflicts: Byzantium; Fatimids; Normans; Italian maritime cities.
polities.leaders: Kalbid emirs; later local qaids
polities.religion: Sunni Islam with Christian and Jewish communities.
polities.culture: Arabic–Greek–Latin contact zone; irrigated agriculture.

polities.name: Norman / Hohenstaufen Sicily

1100.notes: Norman Kingdom of Sicily: island + Apulia/Calabria (from 1130).

1200.notes: Hohenstaufen Kingdom of Sicily under Frederick II.

polities.description: Hauteville Normans forge a multicultural kingdom of Sicily (Roger II) uniting the island with southern Italy. Hohenstaufen inheritance under Frederick II makes Palermo an imperial hub. Angevin conquest (1266) and Sicilian Vespers (1282) split Naples and Sicily.
polities.conflicts: Byzantium; papacy; Tunis; later Angevins vs Aragon.
polities.leaders: Robert Guiscard; Roger II; William II; Frederick II
polities.religion: Latin Christianity ruling Greek Orthodox and Muslim subjects.
polities.culture: Latin–Greek–Arabic chancery; royal assizes; Mediterranean trade.

polities.name: Kingdom of Naples

1300.notes: Angevin / later Aragonese Kingdom of Naples (peninsula).

1400.notes: Angevin / later Aragonese Kingdom of Naples (peninsula).

polities.description: Angevin mainland kingdom after the Vespers separates Sicily (Aragonese). Naples is a major Italian power under Robert of Anjou and later contested by Durazzo and Aragonese claimants.
polities.conflicts: Aragon/Sicily; papacy; Hungarian Angevins; Italian condottieri.
polities.leaders: Charles I of Anjou; Robert of Anjou; Joanna I; Ladislaus
polities.culture: French-Italian court culture; university of Naples.

polities.name: Republic of Venice

1000.notes: Republic of Venice lagoon + early Terraferma; overseas empire not fully drawn.

1100.notes: Republic of Venice lagoon + early Terraferma; overseas empire not fully drawn.

1200.notes: Venice: lagoon, Terraferma beginnings, Adriatic footholds.

1300.notes: Venice: lagoon, Terraferma beginnings, Adriatic footholds.

1400.notes: Venice: lagoon, Terraferma beginnings, Adriatic footholds.

polities.description: Lagoon republic pivots from Byzantine vassalage to independent maritime empire. Fourth Crusade spoils and Stato da Màr colonies (Crete, Negropont, later more) enrich the Rialto. Terraferma expansion intensifies in the 14th–15th centuries versus Milan.
polities.conflicts: Byzantium; Genoa; Hungary (Dalmatia); Ottomans later; Padua/Verona.
polities.leaders: Doges (e.g. Enrico Dandolo); Council of Ten era institutions
polities.religion: Latin Christianity; strong ducal/saint Mark cult.
polities.culture: Venetian Italian; merchant oligarchy; Arsenal shipyards.

polities.name: Republic of Genoa

approx.notes: Republic of Genoa; Ligurian coast + Black Sea colonies offline.
Republic of Genoa; Ligurian coast + Black Sea colonies offline.
Republic of Genoa; Ligurian coast + Black Sea colonies offline.
Republic of Genoa; Ligurian coast + Black Sea colonies offline.

polities.description: Ligurian maritime commune rivals Venice across the Mediterranean and Black Sea (Pera, Caffa). Banking and colonial trade flourish despite chronic factional strife and subordination episodes to Milan/France.
polities.conflicts: Venice; Pisa; Aragon; Milan; Muslim Maghreb/Levant.
polities.leaders: Consuls and doges of the commune; admiral lineages (Doria)
polities.culture: Ligurian Italian; overseas fondachi; naval entrepreneurship.

polities.name: Lombard / Padan communes

1100.notes: Lombard/Padan communal belt (Milan, etc.) — not a single state.

1200.notes: Lombard/Padan communal belt (Milan, etc.) — not a single state.

1300.notes: Lombard/Padan communal belt (Milan, etc.) — not a single state.

polities.description: Self-governing cities of the Po valley (Milan, Verona, Padua, Bologna orbit) form leagues against emperors—most famously the Lombard League vs Barbarossa (Legnano 1176). Later signorie replace many communes.
polities.conflicts: Holy Roman Emperors; papacy (Guelph/Ghibelline); neighboring communes.
polities.leaders: City consuls; later signori (e.g. early Visconti)
polities.culture: Communal statutes; merchant guilds; Romance dialects.

polities.name: Duchy / Lordship of Milan

1400.notes: Visconti Milanese state in the Po valley.

polities.description: Visconti signoria consolidates Lombardy into a territorial state; Gian Galeazzo Visconti nearly unifies northern Italy before 1402. Milan is the Po valley’s dominant land power opposite Venice.
polities.conflicts: Venice; Florence; papacy; Empire.
polities.leaders: Ottone Visconti; Gian Galeazzo Visconti
polities.culture: Lombard industry; condottieri armies; Gothic-Visconti patronage.

polities.name: Republic of Florence
polities.description: Tuscan commune becomes a banking and wool power (florin). Guelf politics, Ciompi revolt (1378), and early Medici influence (after 1400) frame a cultural takeoff toward the Renaissance.
polities.conflicts: Milan; Pisa; Siena; papacy; Empire factions.
polities.leaders: Priorate oligarchs; later Medici (Cosimo after 1434)
polities.culture: Tuscan Italian; guild republic; early humanism.

polities.name: Kievan Rus’

1000.notes: Kievan Rus’ federation of principalities (schematic max extent).

1100.notes: Kievan Rus’ federation of principalities (schematic max extent).

polities.description: Rurikid federation centered on Kiev, Christianized under Vladimir (988) and Yaroslav the Wise. Dynastic appanage fragmentation accelerates in the 12th century; Mongol sack of Kiev (1240) ends the classic order.
polities.conflicts: Pechenegs/Cumans; Poland; Byzantium; steppe nomads; later Mongols.
polities.leaders: Vladimir the Great; Yaroslav the Wise; Vladimir Monomakh
polities.culture: East Slavic; Varangian–Slavic elite fusion; river trade (Baltic–Black Sea).

polities.name: Novgorod Republic

1200.notes: Novgorod Republic / land of Novgorod.

1300.notes: Novgorod Republic / land of Novgorod.

1400.notes: Novgorod Republic / land of Novgorod.

polities.description: Northern Rus’ vector with veche politics, boyar oligarchy, and Hansa trade. Controls vast forest tribute zones toward the White Sea and Urals; contests Sweden and Livonian knights on the Baltic frontier (Alexander Nevsky memory).
polities.conflicts: Vladimir-Suzdal/Moscow; Sweden; Teutonic/Livonian Order; Mongol suzerainty politics.
polities.leaders: Posadniks; archbishops; Alexander Nevsky (prince)
polities.culture: Old East Slavic; fur/wax/honey trade; literacy (birchbark).

polities.name: Vladimir–Suzdal

1200.notes: Vladimir–Suzdal / northeast Rus’ principalities.

1300.notes: Vladimir–Suzdal / northeast Rus’ principalities.

polities.description: Northeast Rus’ power center after Kiev’s decline (Andrei Bogolyubsky, Vsevolod). Mongol invasion subordinates princes; later leadership migrates toward Moscow.
polities.conflicts: Novgorod; Volga Bulgars; Mongols; rival Rurikids.
polities.leaders: Yuri Dolgorukiy; Andrei Bogolyubsky; Vsevolod the Big Nest
polities.culture: East Slavic; white-stone churches; forest colonization.

polities.name: Galicia–Volhynia

1200.notes: Kingdom of Galicia–Volhynia (Ruthenia).

1300.notes: Kingdom of Galicia–Volhynia (Ruthenia).

polities.description: Western Rus’ kingdom under Roman and Daniil, balancing Hungary, Poland, and the Horde. Eventually partitioned by Poland and Lithuania in the 14th century.
polities.conflicts: Hungary; Poland; Mongols; Lithuania; Teutonic politics.
polities.leaders: Roman Mstislavich; Daniil Romanovich
polities.culture: Ruthenian elite; crossroads trade.

polities.name: Golden Horde

1300.notes: Golden Horde steppe dominion over Rus’ tribute zone (western edge).

1400.notes: Golden Horde steppe dominion over Rus’ tribute zone (western edge).

polities.description: Jochid Mongol-Turkic khanate ruling the Pontic–Caspian steppe and extracting tribute from Rus’ princes. Capital Sarai; Islamization under Özbeg. Western edge presses Lithuania, Hungary memories, and Byzantine/Black Sea trade.
polities.conflicts: Rus’ principalities; Lithuania; Ilkhanate; Mamluks (diplomacy); Timur.
polities.leaders: Batu; Berke; Özbeg; Tokhtamysh
polities.culture: Turkic–Mongol steppe; sedentary tribute cities; yarlyk patents to Rus’ princes.

polities.name: Grand Principality of Moscow

1400.notes: Grand Principality of Moscow rising under Dmitry Donskoy / Vasily I.

polities.description: Moscow rises under Mongol suzerainty by collecting tribute and defeating rivals. Dmitry Donskoy’s Kulikovo (1380) is symbolic; Vasily I navigates Lithuania and the Horde. By 1400 Muscovy is the leading northeast Rus’ principality.
polities.conflicts: Golden Horde; Lithuania; Tver; Novgorod; Ryazan.
polities.leaders: Ivan I Kalita; Dmitry Donskoy; Vasily I
polities.religion: Eastern Orthodoxy; Metropolitan transfer toward Moscow.
polities.culture: East Slavic; fortress kremlins; boyar service.

polities.name: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

1200.notes: Early Lithuanian tribal confederation consolidating.

1300.notes: Gediminid Lithuania expanding into Ruthenia.

1400.notes: Grand Duchy of Lithuania at late-medieval expanse; union with Poland.

polities.description: Baltic pagan polity consolidates under Mindaugas (crowned 1253) then expands massively under Gediminas and Algirdas into Ruthenian Orthodox lands. Jogaila’s baptism and Polish union (1385–86) remake it as a Catholic–Orthodox composite giant opposing the Teutonic Order.
polities.conflicts: Teutonic Order; Poland (then union); Golden Horde; Moscow; Galicia rivals.
polities.leaders: Mindaugas; Gediminas; Algirdas; Kęstutis; Jogaila; Vytautas
polities.religion: Baltic paganism into late 14th c.; then Catholic rulers over Orthodox majority east.
polities.culture: Lithuanian dynastic elite; Ruthenian chancery language; multiethnic host.

polities.name: Teutonic Order (Prussia)

1300.notes: Teutonic Order Prussia + Livonian orbit schematic.

1400.notes: Teutonic Order Prussia + Livonian orbit schematic.

polities.description: German military order transferred from the Holy Land to the Baltic crusade against Prussians and later Lithuania. Builds a monastic state with Marienburg capital; clashes with Poland–Lithuania culminate near Grunwald/Tannenberg (1410).
polities.conflicts: Prussian tribes; Lithuania; Poland; Novgorod (Livonian branch).
polities.leaders: Hermann von Salza; later Grand Masters (e.g. Winrich von Kniprode)
polities.culture: German settlers; Ordensstaat administration; Baltic ports.

polities.name: Prussian & Baltic tribes

1000.notes: Old Prussian / Baltic tribal lands before full Teutonic conquest.

1100.notes: Old Prussian / Baltic tribal lands before full Teutonic conquest.

1200.notes: Old Prussian / Baltic tribal lands before full Teutonic conquest.

polities.description: Old Prussians, related Baltic peoples, and neighboring Curonians/Semigallians resist Christian crusades until the Teutonic and Livonian orders subjugate the coasts in the 13th century.
polities.conflicts: Poland; Teutonic Order; Lithuania; Denmark (Estonia).
polities.leaders: Tribal leadership (no single durable monarchy)
polities.culture: Baltic languages; hillfort societies; amber trade memory.

polities.name: Cuman–Kipchak confederation

1100.notes: Cuman–Kipchak confederation on the Pontic steppe.

1200.notes: Cuman–Kipchak confederation on the Pontic steppe.

polities.description: Turkic nomad confederation dominating the Pontic steppe after Pechenegs, raiding and allying with Rus’, Hungary, and Byzantium. Mongol conquest incorporates many Cumans; others flee to Hungary (Kun).
polities.conflicts: Kievan Rus’; Byzantium; Hungary; Georgia; Mongols.
polities.leaders: Khan lineages (e.g. Köten in Hungarian refuge tradition)
polities.religion: Tengrist / shamanic; partial Christianization of refugees.
polities.culture: Turkic steppe pastoralism; heavy cavalry.

polities.name: Crusader states (Outremer)

1100.notes: First Crusade states: Jerusalem, Antioch, Edessa (Tripoli nearby).

1200.notes: Reduced Levantine crusader footholds + Lusignan Cyprus.

1300.notes: Acre falls 1291; Cyprus remains the main Latin East kingdom.

polities.description: First Crusade creates Jerusalem, Antioch, Edessa, and Tripoli. Edessa falls 1144; Jerusalem 1187 (Hattin) to Saladin; Acre and the last Levantine footholds fall 1291. Lusignan Cyprus remains a Latin kingdom into the later Middle Ages.
polities.conflicts: Fatimids; Seljuks; Zengids; Ayyubids; Mamluks; Byzantium; Mongols.
polities.leaders: Godfrey of Bouillon; Baldwin I; Bohemond; later Lusignans; Louis IX as crusader
polities.religion: Latin Catholicism over Muslim and Eastern Christian majorities.
polities.culture: French feudal imports; Italian communes in ports; military orders (Temple, Hospital).

polities.name: Swiss Confederation

1300.notes: Swiss Confederation cantons emerging from Habsburg conflict.

1400.notes: Swiss Confederation cantons emerging from Habsburg conflict.

polities.description: Forest cantons (Uri, Schwyz, Unterwalden) ally in 1291 and expand after Morgarten (1315) and Sempach (1386) against Habsburgs. By 1400 an autonomous confederation exists inside/against the Reich framework.
polities.conflicts: Habsburgs; Burgundy later; Milan later.
polities.leaders: Cantonal landamänner; legendary Tell cycle (later tradition)
polities.culture: German (and later Romance) alpine communities; infantry reputation.

polities.name: Principality of Wallachia

1400.notes: Principality of Wallachia (from c. 1330).

polities.description: Romanian principality south of the Carpathians under Basarab I, navigating Hungarian suzerainty claims and rising Ottoman pressure. Strategic Danube frontier state by 1400.
polities.conflicts: Hungary; Ottomans; Bulgaria remnants; Moldavia twin politics.
polities.leaders: Basarab I; later Mircea the Elder (nearby in time)
polities.culture: Romanian elite; mixed pastoral-agricultural economy.

polities.name: Icelandic Commonwealth

1000.notes: Icelandic Commonwealth → later Norwegian dominion.

1100.notes: Icelandic Commonwealth → later Norwegian dominion.

1200.notes: Icelandic Commonwealth → later Norwegian dominion.

polities.description: Godar-led commonwealth with Althing law; Christianized c. 1000. Sturlung Age civil conflict ends with submission to the Norwegian crown (Old Covenant 1262–64).
polities.conflicts: Internal chieftain feuds; Norwegian royal pressure.
polities.leaders: Lawspeakers; Sturlung leaders; saga-age chieftains
polities.culture: Old Norse; saga literature; pastoral farms.
